test_cases.title: validate_range accepts 7d, 30d, and 90d and the endpoint scopes its query accordingly
test_cases.given: a test FastAPI router built on Depends(validate_range) that echoes the resolved range and the query scope it derived
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called with range=7d, range=30d, and range=90d in turn
test_cases.then: each call succeeds with 200 and the response reports the range value was accepted and used to scope the query
test_cases.objective: Verify all three documented range values are accepted by the shared dependency and reach the handler for query scoping.
preconditions: app/dependencies/range.py exposes validate_range()
a throwaway test router registers one GET endpoint with range: str = Depends(validate_range)
steps: Mount the test router on a FastAPI TestClient app
GET /test-range?range=7d, then range=30d, then range=90d
expected_results: All three requests return HTTP 200
Each response body echoes the exact range value that was requested
No HTTPException is raised for any of the three accepted values

test_cases.title: Accepted range value maps to the correct lookback-window boundary
test_cases.given: the same test router as TC-01, additionally computing a query start-date from the validated range
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called with each accepted range value against a fixed 'now' clock
test_cases.then: the computed start-date is exactly now minus the range's day count (7, 30, or 90)
test_cases.objective: Verify range acceptance actually scopes the query window correctly, not just that the string passes validation.
preconditions: Test endpoint freezes 'now' to a fixed timestamp for deterministic assertions
steps: Freeze the clock to test_data.frozen_now
Call the test endpoint with range=7d, 30d, and 90d in turn
Read the computed start-date from each response
expected_results: Computed start-date for each range matches test_data.expected_start exactly

test_cases.title: Range values outside {7d, 30d, 90d} return HTTP 400, never FastAPI's default 422
test_cases.given: the same test router built on Depends(validate_range)
test_cases.when: the endpoint is called with a range value not in {7d, 30d, 90d}
test_cases.then: the response status is 400, not the FastAPI/Pydantic default 422 type-coercion error
test_cases.objective: Verify the explicit-check mechanism (Depends raising HTTPException(400) before Pydantic coercion) rejects out-of-set values with 400, closing the 400-vs-422 gap FastAPI would otherwise produce.
preconditions: validate_range() runs as a Depends() function, not inline per-handler or middleware
steps: For each value in test_data.invalid_values, GET /test-range?range=<value>
Record the response status code for each call
expected_results: Every call in test_data.invalid_values returns status_code == 400
No call returns 422 for any of the five values, including the case-sensitivity variant '7D'

test_cases.title: Invalid range rejection returns the exact error_body() envelope shape via register_exception_handlers()
test_cases.given: validate_range() raises HTTPException(400, 'invalid_range') for a value outside {7d, 30d, 90d}
test_cases.when: the request is handled by an app with register_exception_handlers() wired (app/core/errors.py)
test_cases.then: the response body is exactly {"error": {"code": "http_400", "message": "invalid_range", "details": null}}
test_cases.objective: Verify FR-1's exact mechanism: validate_range() routes through the existing error_body()/register_exception_handlers() machinery, producing the documented envelope byte-for-byte, not an ad hoc shape.
preconditions: Test app calls register_exception_handlers(app) from app/core/errors.py
Test router depends on validate_range()
steps: GET /test-range?range=60d against the wired test app
Parse the JSON response body
expected_results: response.status_code == 400
response.json() == {"error": {"code": "http_400", "message": "invalid_range", "details": null}}

test_cases.title: JSONFormatter surfaces extra={route, param, rejected_value} fields in the emitted JSON payload
test_cases.given: a logging.LogRecord created via logger.warning('invalid_range', extra={'route': ..., 'param': ..., 'rejected_value': ...}) formatted by JSONFormatter
test_cases.when: JSONFormatter.format(record) is called and the result parsed as JSON
test_cases.then: the parsed payload contains route, param, and rejected_value keys with the exact values passed in extra
test_cases.objective: Verify FR-3: JSONFormatter.format merges LogRecord extras into its JSON payload. This test MUST fail against the current formatter (which builds its payload from a fixed key set and never reads record.__dict__) and MUST pass once the extra-passthrough merge is added.
preconditions: app/core/logging.py's JSONFormatter importable
A logging.LogRecord can be constructed directly (bypassing a real logger) or captured via a test logging.Handler
steps: Create a LogRecord (or emit via a captured logger.warning call) with extra=test_data
Call JSONFormatter().format(record)
json.loads() the returned string
expected_results: Parsed payload['route'] == '/api/activities'
Parsed payload['param'] == 'range'
Parsed payload['rejected_value'] == '60d'

test_cases.title: JSONFormatter extras merge excludes standard/reserved LogRecord attributes
test_cases.given: a LogRecord formatted by JSONFormatter with no custom extra fields supplied
test_cases.when: JSONFormatter.format(record) is called and the result parsed as JSON
test_cases.then: the parsed payload contains only the documented fixed keys (timestamp, level, logger, message, exc_info?) plus any genuine extras — never internal LogRecord attributes like pathname, funcName, or args leaking in as top-level keys
test_cases.objective: Prove the extras-merge added for FR-3 does not also leak Python's standard LogRecord attribute set, which would pollute the JSON payload and could collide with future extra field names.
preconditions: app/core/logging.py's JSONFormatter importable
steps: Emit a plain logger.warning('test message') with no extra kwarg
Call JSONFormatter().format(record) on the resulting LogRecord
json.loads() the returned string
expected_results: None of test_data.reserved_attrs_to_check appear as top-level keys in the parsed payload
Parsed payload only contains timestamp, level, logger, message (and exc_info only when an exception is present)

Test app wires the real validate_range() dependency on one endpoint
